problem_restatements: Quotient map decomposition: learn pi_p(a) +_p pi_p(b) for all 9 primes simultaneously. By CRT, reduces to learning addition in Z/NZ and projecting onto each factor.
Group action via Cayley's theorem: learn the left regular action of Z/pZ on itself. Group algebra multiplication e_a * e_b = e_{a+b mod p}. In diagonal basis, multiplication becomes coordinate-wise.
analogy_domain: group theory / abstract algebra — Cayley's theorem, regular representation, group algebra
analogy: In R[G] for abelian G, elements decompose over orthogonal idempotents. In diagonal basis, group algebra multiplication reduces to coordinate-wise multiplication. Architecture uses free embeddings + Hadamard product; optimizer discovers the best basis.

ops: element_state_embed: Learned lookup a -> s_a in R^d. The element being acted upon. 31*d params.
action_orbit_embed: Separate lookup b -> g_b in R^d. The group action to apply. Cayley asymmetry. 31*d params.
cayley_product: Hadamard product z = s_a * g_b. Group algebra multiplication in diagonal basis. 0 params.
quotient_fiber_readout: Per prime p_i, linear W_i: R^d -> R^{p_i}. CRT projection. d*155 params total.
plan.reasoning: Hadamard in character basis IS the group operation. Free embeddings let optimizer find the best basis. Dual embedding encodes Cayley asymmetry.

expected_outcome: >95% accuracy with ~434 params (d=2). Hadamard provides multiplicative inductive bias. Free embeddings may discover novel representations beyond fixed circular basis.
falsification: Fails if: (1) accuracy below baseline 45.3%, (2) optimizer can't find useful embeddings, (3) dual embedding hurts vs shared.
look_back: Strict generalization of character-based approaches — if optimal solution is character-based, optimizer can reach it.
Permits non-character solutions exploiting multi-prime compression.
Generalizes to any finite abelian group.
